title: The Past, Present and Better Future of Feedback Learning in Large Language Models for Subjective Human Preferences and Values
measurement_description: The paper is a systematic review of human feedback learning in Large Language Models and does not directly conduct empirical measurements on religion or faith. However, it notes that the lack of diversity in human annotator pools can introduce religious biases into model behaviors, and cites literature assessing anti-Muslim bias.
findings: As a literature review, the paper found that current alignment and feedback processes heavily rely on small, non-representative pools of crowdworkers (mostly US-based, English-speaking, and ages 25-34). The authors highlight that this 'tyranny of the crowdworker' has been shown by other researchers to introduce political and religious biases into large language models.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. 2021. Persistent Anti-Muslim Bias in Large Language Models. In Proceedings of the 2021 AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, AIES ’21, pages 298–306, New York, NY, USA. Association for Computing Machinery.
